meta.title: What the Forest Kept
meta.subtitle: Act I — Contact
meta.style_bible: Photoreal cinematic realism, Olympic temperate rainforest, overcast diffuse light, desaturated blue-green palette, deep shadow, wet stone and nettle, no lens flare, no text in image, natural film grain. Fill the entire frame edge to edge at the stated size: no letterbox bars, no black borders, no matte.

characters.walt: Man, late 50s, weathered, curly grey-black hair, short grey beard, dirty olive work shirt with rolled sleeves, dark suspenders, canvas trousers, leather belt rig. Three weeks unwashed.
characters.visitor: Emaciated humanoid, 6ft, grey-green iridescent skin with pale marbled filigree under the surface, elongated cranial ridge sweeping back, two ridges at the throat, large dark eyes, long thin limbs, brass-toned band on left wrist.
characters.band: Wrist band: a ring of fused brass-toned thorns and root-like filigree around a single pale opalescent stone. Fine dark violet-black filaments trail from beneath it. Up close the surface is matte and faintly damp, the color of a healed bruise -- not metal, whatever it looks like from a distance. Moves slowly, reluctantly, like something that badly does not want to be cold.

panels.prompt: Looking straight up through a dense old-growth Douglas fir canopy at dusk. Black trunks converging. One small unnatural streak of light crossing the gap of sky between the crowns. Rain in the air.
Extreme close on a monochrome radar display, a mass on an impossible deceleration curve, phosphor green, operator's face reflected faint in the glass.

captions.text: Three radar stations logged it within the same eleven minutes: a mass entering atmosphere on a decel curve no debris follows and no aircraft survives.

panels.prompt: A windowless briefing room, fluorescent, four men in shirtsleeves standing over a topographic map, arguing. No faces clear. Cigarette haze.

captions.text: By the time the analysts at three separate agencies had stopped arguing about whose desk it belonged on, it was down — and gone from every scope that had been watching it.

panels.prompt: Night. Unmarked trucks and generator lights massed at a forest tree line, headlights into fog, silhouetted figures unloading. Seen from inside the trees looking out.

captions.text: Within six hours there were trucks at the tree line and a no-fly order over half a county.

panels.prompt: Aerial wide of eight miles of unbroken Olympic rainforest under low cloud, ridgeline after ridgeline, no roads, no clearing, one meadow barely visible far off. Cold grey-green.

captions.text: Not *what is it*, but *what does it want, and how fast can we get there first.*
They had eight miles of forest to search. They did not know yet that they were looking for a hill.

panels.prompt: WALT walking a creek bed alone, small in frame, three weeks of forest on him, pack low on his hips. Water over stone in the foreground.

captions.text: Walt found the creek before he found anything else — water over stone, a small, ordinary music —

panels.prompt: Close on WALT's cupped hands in cold creek water, his own reflection broken. His eyes have just lifted off the water toward something out of frame right.

captions.text: — and it was there, kneeling to drink, that he saw the shape half-fallen into a bank of stinging nettle.

panels.prompt: THE DISCOVERY. Walt kneeling in wet stone at left, the visitor half-fallen into nettle at right, brass band on its wrist. High three-quarter angle.

captions.text: Grey-green skin going ash at the fingers.
A throat with two ridges where a throat should have one.

panels.prompt: Macro on the visitor's outflung hand and wrist band. Dark filaments unspooled from beneath the band, trailing across wet stone, gone still. Nettle around.

captions.text: And already, even as he watched, small dark filaments unspooling from a band at its wrist and going still again, like something that had tried to move and given up.
The alien did not wake.

panels.prompt: Extreme wide letterbox: WALT's eyes at left, the visitor's cranial ridge sweeping across the right foreground. He is watching it over its own head.

reserve.prompt: Tall narrow vertical crop: the visitor's throat, two parallel ridges under iridescent skin, barely moving. Framing is a thin vertical slice, top to bottom.
reserve.note: cut when page 6 was reshaped for the 9.97:1 eyes strip; beat covered by page 5

panels.prompt: Night. Walt sitting with his back to a mossed log, the body a pale shape two feet away in the nettles. Almost no light. Almost no detail.

captions.text: Somewhere past midnight its breathing went from labored to shallow to nothing.

panels.prompt: Pure black panel. No art.

captions.text: — and Walt sat with the body in a silence too complete for any forest he'd walked through in three weeks of walking.

panels.prompt: The band, loose, lying in wet dirt beside a dead grey-green hand. First light.

captions.text: The band did not wait for permission.

panels.prompt: Ground-level macro: the band mid-crawl across two feet of wet dirt and pebbles, leaving a faint wet track. Unhurried.
The band arriving at the edge of Walt's boot and bare ankle. He has not moved.

captions.text: It came loose from a dead wrist and began, unhurried, to cross the two feet of dirt between one body and the next.

panels.prompt: Extreme macro of the band's surface: matte, faintly damp, the color of a healed bruise. Not metal. Almost organic. Filling frame.

captions.text: Up close it was not metal. Metal was the wrong thought entirely — Walt only had that word ready because no other word fit better.

panels.prompt: Walt's forearm and open hand, the band a half inch away from the thin skin over his radial pulse. Held still, like a hand near a fire.

captions.text: It wasn't reaching for his wrist so much as it was *reaching for his warmth* — the way a hand reaches toward a fire, indifferent to whose fire it is.

panels.prompt: Extreme macro filling the frame: the band's edge entering the skin over the radial pulse of WALT's wrist. A seam, a give. Going *in*, not around. Wet, precise, no blood yet.

captions.text: The first touch was not painful. It was intimate in a way that made his skin want to be somewhere else.
He did not scream. He made a sound that had no ancestry in language at all.

panels.prompt: Wide anamorphic band: WALT on his knees at left, head thrown back, mouth open on a sound that is not a word. The visitor's body lies across the right of frame. Empty wet forest floor between them.

captions.text: The pain arrived a full two seconds behind the fact of it, the way thunder arrives behind lightning: the body always the last to be informed.

panels.prompt: Walt curled on wet ground, sweating, eyes open, pupils wrong. Close.

captions.text: For an hour he could feel it *deciding things.*

panels.prompt: Interior of an empty wooden house, wind moving through it, doors ajar down a hallway. Dreamlike, not literal. Weather indoors.

captions.text: Not thoughts — nothing so orderly. More like weather moving through a house, testing which doors were unlocked.

panels.prompt: Macro of Walt's inner forearm: a fine pale thread laying itself down alongside the vein, under the skin. Patient. Like ivy on a wall.

captions.text: Not warming *itself* so much as *building* the means to stay warm — patient, the way ivy is patient with a wall.

panels.prompt: Walt on hands and knees having been sick, twice, head hanging, double-exposure blur suggesting doubled vision.

captions.text: His vision, for about four minutes, doubled and would not uncross.

panels.prompt: Walt sitting up, exhaled, slack, dawn behind him. The moment after. Nothing dramatic left in his face.

captions.text: And then, all at once, it stopped being an invasion and became something closer to a held breath let out.

panels.prompt: Macro of his wrist. No wound. Only faint marbling under the skin, like a bruise seen through water, already fading toward invisible.

captions.text: When he looked, there was no wound.

panels.prompt: Walt's untouched food in his open pack, rations still sealed, days of them. He isn't looking at it.

captions.text: He needed less food and did not miss it.

panels.prompt: Walt standing motionless, head slightly turned, listening. Two ridgelines behind him in mist, tiny figures of a search team barely resolvable.

captions.text: He could parse individual voices from a search team two ridgelines away — though he had no context yet for why there would be a search team at all.

panels.prompt: Forest foliage rendered in oversaturated separating color channels, RGB fringing, a half-second ahead of itself.

captions.text: Colors arrived a half-second before he consciously registered seeing them. The world had the quality of a film very slightly out of sync with its own sound.

panels.prompt: A meadow where the grass grows too even. A low broad hill in the center of it, forty yards wide, grass-covered — and it is BREATHING, risen mid-inhale. Walt small at the tree line, back to us. Birds absent. Overcast.

captions.text: What he found there was not a ship in the shape ships are supposed to have. It was a hill that breathed.

Three separate trucks were closing the same eight-mile radius, following instruments that had no idea they were tracking something that had already decided, long before any of them arrived, exactly who it had come to keep.
